channel.title: Insights Aggregator
channel.description: Investment insights from banks & asset managers, aggregated.

item.title: US Rates: And you’re not gonna reach my telephone
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · At Any Rate — JPMorgan researchers discuss the latest US inflation data and its implications for rates markets. The podcast analyzes recent economic indicators and explores how inflation trends are shaping interest rate expectations and market positioning.

item.title: Global Data Pod Weekender: September song
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · Global Data Pod — Major central banks including the ECB, Fed, and BoJ implemented rate hikes in September 2026, marking what JPMorgan economists characterize as the beginning of a broad tightening cycle after a period of easing. This represents a significant shift in monetary policy direction across the world's largest economies.

item.title: Why the Middle-Class Squeeze Is Getting Worse
item.dc:creator: Morgan Stanley
item.description: Morgan Stanley · Thoughts on the Market — A Morgan Stanley economics discussion explores how the American middle class is being squeezed by rising essential costs while wealth divergence creates a K-shaped economy. The analysis examines how factors like inflation in necessities and artificial intelligence development are reshaping household finances and financial security across income levels.

item.title: Mixed Markets, Fed Feels Hike Heat (E276)
item.dc:creator: DoubleLine
item.description: DoubleLine · DoubleLine Minutes — DoubleLine's portfolio managers reviewed market activity during a shortened holiday week in early September, noting mixed performance across asset classes. The discussion covered central bank policy pressures and market reactions to Fed rate trajectory expectations. Trading volumes were lighter due to the holiday calendar.

item.title: Global FX: Post-CPI and pre-Fed FX round up
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · At Any Rate — JPMorgan researchers analyze foreign exchange market dynamics following the latest US CPI release and ahead of the Federal Reserve's policy decision. The discussion evaluates currency resilience across different scenarios, particularly within a potential hiking cycle, and examines the implications for global FX markets.

item.title: Global Rates: Dissecting the sell-off in European rates, next week’s BoE meeting
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · At Any Rate — JPMorgan analysts discuss the recent decline in European government bond yields and preview the upcoming Bank of England monetary policy decision scheduled for September 2026. The conversation examines the drivers behind the eurozone rate sell-off and implications for UK policy direction.

item.title: Global Data Pod: The ECB is on the move, will the BoE follow?
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · Global Data Pod — The ECB has taken a hawkish stance on monetary policy, and analysts are examining whether the Bank of England will adopt a similarly hawkish approach in its upcoming decision. The discussion explores the implications of coordinated or divergent central bank actions across major economies.

item.title: The Week Ahead - Crunch time for the Fed and the BOJ
item.dc:creator: Nomura
item.description: Nomura · Nomura — The Week Ahead — Central banks face critical decisions this week as bond markets show vulnerability. The Federal Reserve will address August CPI data and provide guidance, while the BOJ meets alongside important economic data from China and India. European central banks including the ECB and BOE also have significant decisions on tap.

item.title: Cross Asset Research – Societe Generale
item.dc:creator: Société Générale
item.description: Société Générale · SG Cross Asset Research (web) — Société Générale's Cross Asset Research team provides integrated analysis spanning multiple asset classes including equities, fixed income, commodities, and currencies. The research examines macroeconomic developments and their implications for portfolio positioning across global markets.

item.title: View from the markets: Tightening again – EN
item.dc:creator: BNP Paribas
item.description: BNP Paribas · BNPP AM Viewpoint (web) — Central banks are resuming rate increases amid geopolitical tensions from the Iran conflict that began in February. The European Central Bank raised rates this week, with markets expecting similar moves from the Federal Reserve and Bank of England. Investors are favoring floating rate debt, high yield bonds, and shorter-duration inflation-linked bonds over longer-term fixed-rate securities in this tightening environment.

item.title: What comes next for European markets?
item.dc:creator: RBC Capital Markets
item.description: RBC Capital Markets · Macro Minutes — RBC Capital Markets discusses emerging opportunities in European markets amid ongoing changes and explains how the firm is enhancing its capabilities across people, products, and technology to serve clients more effectively. The episode highlights RBC's European expertise and commitment to delivering solutions that help clients navigate evolving market conditions.

item.title: Cross Asset Research – Societe Generale
item.dc:creator: Société Générale
item.description: Société Générale · SG Cross Asset Research (web) — Société Générale's Cross Asset Research provides analysis spanning multiple asset classes, including equities, fixed income, currencies, and commodities. The division publishes regular insights, research publications, and video content to inform investment decision-making across global markets.

item.title: Sustainable Funds Beat Traditional Funds in 2026
item.dc:creator: Morgan Stanley
item.description: Morgan Stanley · MS Insights (web) — Sustainable funds outperformed traditional funds in the first half of 2026, with the asset class reaching a record $4.24 trillion in total assets despite experiencing only modest inflows during the period.

item.title: 25 Years of Benchmark-Free Investing
item.dc:creator: GMO
item.description: GMO · GMO Research Library & 7-Year Forecast (web) — Ben Inker discusses GMO's 25-year history of benchmark-independent asset allocation, examining how the firm's approach has evolved and the principles that guide investment decisions outside traditional index constraints. He considers how current market conditions may present opportunities for investors willing to deviate from conventional benchmarks.

item.title: The future of treasury: From back office to strategic forefront
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · Making Sense — Treasury functions are evolving from operational back-office roles into strategic business drivers that enhance resilience and growth. The discussion examines how technology, real-time data, and AI are transforming treasury operations, along with the evolving skill requirements for treasury leaders seeking to generate competitive advantage through data-driven insights.

item.title: 270: Sports, Markets and Investing: What Separates Skill From Good Luck
item.dc:creator: BlackRock
item.description: BlackRock · The Bid — This episode explores parallels between elite sports and investing, examining how small statistical edges compound through repeated decisions and strong processes. The discussion covers hit rates, payoff ratios, teamwork and preparation in both domains, using examples from tennis, soccer and basketball to illustrate decision-making principles applicable to fixed income portfolio management.

item.title: How Automation Impacts the Lives and Careers of Displaced Workers
item.dc:creator: Goldman Sachs
item.description: Goldman Sachs · GS Insights (web) — Historical technology waves reveal how automation displaces workers and the varying effectiveness of retraining programs in helping them transition. The analysis examines past technological shifts to understand labor market impacts and policy responses that support displaced workers.

item.title: What a Fed Rate Hike Could Mean for US Stocks
item.dc:creator: Goldman Sachs
item.description: Goldman Sachs · GS Insights (web) — Goldman Sachs' Jonathan Shugar discusses how a Federal Reserve rate hike might affect US stock market performance, suggesting that rate increases may not necessarily prevent equity market gains. The analysis explores the relationship between monetary policy tightening and equity market dynamics.

item.title: The Quant Renaissance Part III: Who's Ready for the Next Winter?
item.dc:creator: Man Group
item.description: Man Group · Man Institute Insights — The analysis examines whether quantitative fund managers improved their strategies and performance following the 2007-2008 Quant Winter crisis. Evidence shows mixed results, with some quant managers demonstrating meaningful adaptation while others have not fundamentally changed their approaches or returns.

item.title: The Fed, Football and the Price of Ambiguity
item.dc:creator: Morgan Stanley
item.description: Morgan Stanley · Thoughts on the Market — Andrew Sheets, Global Head of Fixed Income Research at Morgan Stanley, uses American football's strategic value of ambiguity as an analogy for financial markets. He explores how markets may not adequately price in uncertainty around key themes such as Fed policy, AI financing, and energy supply, drawing parallels to how football teams gain advantage through unpredictability.

item.title: Drawing Comparisons Between Technology Regimes: A Behavioral View
item.dc:creator: PIMCO
item.description: PIMCO · PIMCO Pod — PIMCO compares the current AI investment boom to the dot-com era, exploring behavioral parallels while identifying key differences that could influence investor risk and opportunity profiles. The discussion examines how technology regime shifts historically impact markets and what lessons from past cycles may apply today.

item.title: EM Fixed Income: Battle tested, but shields still up
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · At Any Rate — Anezka Christovova, Ben Ramsey, and Tania Escobedo examine emerging market fixed income dynamics and recent market developments affecting the asset class. The discussion explores how EM fixed income has withstood recent challenges while positioning strategies for current market conditions.

item.title: Strong payrolls support rate hike expectations amid AI-earnings boom
item.dc:creator: Citi
item.description: Citi · Citi Wealth Market Insights (web) — U.S. August non-farm payrolls came in at 162,000, nearly triple consensus expectations, with real wage incomes rising. This strong labor data has led markets to reprice interest rate hike expectations upward, making a September Federal Reserve move increasingly defensible. The combination of robust economic growth, persistent inflation, and higher rates may create headwinds for fixed income investors.

item.title: The Fall Feels
item.dc:creator: RBC Capital Markets
item.description: RBC Capital Markets · RBC's Markets in Motion — RBC Capital Markets updates its US equity market outlook for fall, noting increased near-term pullback risks while maintaining a constructive longer-term view with an 8,150 S&P 500 price target. The firm also reviews recent developments in valuations, flows, capital expenditure, and small-cap performance.

item.title: Gold’s rollercoaster ride
item.dc:creator: HSBC
item.description: HSBC · The Macro Brief — Gold prices have experienced significant volatility throughout the year, driven by various macroeconomic factors. An HSBC precious metals analyst examines the key drivers behind these price swings and discusses the potential for continued volatility moving forward.

item.title: Charting an earnings surge, powered by AI capex
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · AM · Portfolio Insights — U.S. corporate earnings are experiencing significant growth driven by artificial intelligence capital expenditure investments. JPMorgan Asset Management recommends overweighting equities and AI-related opportunities while managing risk through diversified exposure. The report examines the portfolio implications of this earnings trajectory and its connection to AI infrastructure spending.

item.title: UK turns its grid inside-out in its quest for Clean Power 2030
item.dc:creator: RBC Capital Markets
item.description: RBC Capital Markets · Strategic Alternatives — The UK is pursuing an aggressive Clean Power 2030 mission to achieve a predominantly clean electricity system by 2030 through substantial investments in renewable generation, grid infrastructure, and energy storage. The strategy involves a major transmission network overhaul—the largest grid build since the 1960s—to transition from coal-based to wind-powered systems while improving energy security. However, the affordability challenge remains significant as the country must address the mismatch between its clean energy capacity and current electricity demand levels.

item.title: Cross Asset Research – Societe Generale
item.dc:creator: Société Générale
item.description: Société Générale · SG Cross Asset Research (web) — Société Générale's Cross Asset Research provides comprehensive analysis and insights across multiple asset classes and market segments. The platform aggregates their latest research publications, commentary, and video content covering global financial markets. This represents institutional research covering equities, fixed income, currencies, commodities, and macro trends.

item.title: Bond talk: Which way interest rates?
item.dc:creator: Capital Group
item.description: Capital Group · Capital Ideas — A Capital Group fixed income manager provides his perspective on the U.S. bond market outlook amid concerns about elevated inflation and rising debt levels that have triggered a sell-off. The discussion addresses key factors influencing bond valuations and interest rate direction in the current economic environment.

item.title: U.S. vs. international and emerging markets stocks
item.dc:creator: Capital Group
item.description: Capital Group · Capital Group Insights & Outlook (web) — Emerging markets have outperformed U.S. stocks year-to-date, prompting questions about whether this trend can be sustained. The analysis examines the relative performance dynamics between U.S., international developed, and emerging market equities to assess the outlook for each region.

item.title: Final frontier: 6 opportunities in the space economy
item.dc:creator: Capital Group
item.description: Capital Group · Capital Group Insights & Outlook (web) — Capital Group investment professionals identify six opportunities within the emerging space economy, offering analysis on growth prospects while distinguishing between speculative claims and substantive business fundamentals. The space sector encompasses diverse applications from satellite communications to resource exploration, presenting potential investment angles across multiple industries.

item.title: A new paradigm for Emerging Market equities?
item.dc:creator: BNP Paribas
item.description: BNP Paribas · Talking Heads — Emerging market equities are undergoing a structural shift toward technology and manufacturing sectors, driven by AI-related capital spending from major tech companies. BNP Paribas Asset Management experts discuss how this evolution positions emerging markets to benefit from both long-term economic growth and competitive advantages in manufacturing and knowledge-based industries.

item.title: Taking the pulse on medical tourism
item.dc:creator: HSBC
item.description: HSBC · Under the Banyan Tree — Asia's medical tourism sector has evolved significantly beyond basic healthcare services, becoming a substantial and growing business segment. The podcast explores the expansion and modernization of this industry across the region, examining its economic drivers and investment implications.

item.title: Yen In Black
item.dc:creator: State Street
item.description: State Street · Street Signals — The Japanese yen has strengthened after years of anticipated gains, supported by official Japanese intervention and potential U.S. collaboration. The episode explores the drivers of recent yen strength, its sustainability, and potential magnitude of what could become a significant currency trend over the coming period.

item.title: Can AI Earn It Back? The $2 Trillion Test and Other Forces Reshaping Markets and Portfolios
item.dc:creator: Apollo
item.description: Apollo · Apollo Insights & Outlook (web) — Over the next decade, approximately $5 trillion will be invested in AI infrastructure, requiring businesses and consumers to spend $2 trillion annually on AI services to justify the expenditure. The conversation examines whether AI can deliver sufficient returns on this massive investment and its implications for debt and equity markets, alongside exploring US reindustrialization trends and shifts reshaping the financial sector.

item.title: Climate investing in a constrained world
item.dc:creator: Wellington
item.description: Wellington · Wellington Insights & Outlooks (web) — Climate investing opportunities span multiple sectors beyond renewables, including infrastructure, automation, and AI-driven optimization across the physical economy. Innovation and performance improvements in these areas are creating diverse investment pathways to address climate challenges while potentially generating returns. The approach recognizes climate transition as affecting various economic segments and industries.

item.title: Conference Insights: Thoughts from our 2026 Tech Conference
item.dc:creator: Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank · Podzept — Deutsche Bank analysts discuss key takeaways from their 2026 Technology Conference, covering presentations and meetings with tech companies focused on AI, emerging technologies, IT services, and agentic commerce. The conference featured insights from leading technology firms on current market trends and strategic directions in the sector.

item.title: Can the AI Spending Boom Pay Off?
item.dc:creator: Morgan Stanley
item.description: Morgan Stanley · Thoughts on the Market — Major cloud providers are investing over $1.4 trillion in AI infrastructure buildout, with compute capacity expected to quadruple between 2025 and 2028. Morgan Stanley's U.S. Internet analyst examines whether these massive capital investments can generate sufficient returns, identifying business models with potential 25-50 percent returns for Gen-AI-enabled technologies.

item.title: How Will Less Fed Transparency Affect Markets and the Economy?
item.dc:creator: Goldman Sachs
item.description: Goldman Sachs · Goldman Sachs Exchanges — Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh has reduced central bank transparency, and experts debate the implications for markets and economic outcomes. Participants discuss an optimal balance of Fed communication—providing enough information for market function without excessive forward guidance—and whether reduced guidance improves or worsens market signals and volatility dynamics.

item.title: PERSPECTIVES: Economic and asset class outlook – September 2026 | Insights
item.dc:creator: Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank · Deutsche Bank Wealth CIO Insights (web) — Deutsche Bank's Global CIO examines why financial markets have remained resilient amid economic and geopolitical challenges, attributing this to strong corporate earnings and AI-related investments. The analysis covers the macroeconomic environment and its implications for equities, fixed income, gold, and overall portfolio positioning.

item.title: Guarded exuberance in EM FX
item.dc:creator: RBC Capital Markets
item.description: RBC Capital Markets · Macro Minutes — Emerging market FX has benefited from resilient growth and controlled inflation, supporting a constructive macro environment. RBC Capital Markets maintains a bullish stance on select EM currencies including KRW, MYR, and BRL, while cautioning against exposure to rising energy prices and maintaining some hedge positions in the portfolio.

item.title: How is the U.S.-China AI race evolving?
item.dc:creator: JPMorgan
item.description: JPMorgan · AM · Market Insights — The U.S.-China AI competition is evolving with agentic AI and Chinese open-weight models reshaping cost efficiency and enterprise adoption. These developments are altering the competitive dynamics and accessibility of AI technology across both markets. The trends suggest structural shifts in how AI is deployed and commercialized globally.

item.title: Clarity, Access, and Opportunity: Jefferies Unveils Its GCC Index to Capture the New Gulf
item.dc:creator: Jefferies
item.description: Jefferies · Jefferies Insights & Quarterly (web) — Jefferies has launched a new GCC Index designed to provide a benchmark for tracking the six Gulf Cooperation Council nations (Bahrain, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE). The index addresses a gap in institutional investor access to the region's most investable listed companies, as the GCC now controls approximately 40% of global sovereign wealth fund assets and represents a significant emerging markets investment opportunity.

item.title: Capital Market Outlook
item.dc:creator: Bank of America
item.description: Bank of America · BofA Private Bank Insights (web) — BofA Private Bank provides a capital markets outlook as of September 2026, offering perspective on economic conditions and investment positioning across major asset classes. The outlook addresses near-term market dynamics and longer-term strategic considerations for portfolio management.

item.title: Why Momentum Investing Can Still Work
item.dc:creator: BlackRock
item.description: BlackRock · BlackRock Insights & Outlook (web) — BlackRock examines momentum investing strategies and their continued effectiveness in modern markets. The analysis explores how momentum-based approaches can generate returns despite market evolution and changing conditions.

item.title: Why Global Bond Yields Are Expected to Stay Elevated
item.dc:creator: Goldman Sachs
item.description: Goldman Sachs · GS Insights (web) — Goldman Sachs expects global bond yields to remain elevated despite some temporary factors moderating, primarily due to persistent fiscal pressures across developed economies. While certain drivers of higher yields may fade, structural fiscal challenges are anticipated to keep upward pressure on longer-maturity bonds. This suggests a sustained environment of higher yields rather than a return to pre-2021 levels.

item.title: Top of Mind: Challenging false investment dichotomies
item.dc:creator: Wellington
item.description: Wellington · Wellington Insights & Outlooks (web) — A multi-asset strategist challenges three common investment dichotomies: active versus passive management, US versus non-US exposure, and public versus private investments. Rather than viewing these as binary choices, the analysis suggests investors may benefit from more nuanced approaches that combine elements of each category. The piece argues that rigid either/or thinking can limit investment strategy effectiveness.

item.title: Views from the Floor The Mispriced Debt Powering the AI Boom
item.dc:creator: Man Group
item.description: Man Group · Man Institute Insights — Strong demand for data centre financing has created a structural imbalance in the corporate debt market, with borrowing surging to support AI infrastructure buildout. This mismatch between supply and demand for such debt may have created mispricing opportunities in the market.

item.title: AI Debt Starts Moving the U.S. Treasurys Market
item.dc:creator: Morgan Stanley
item.description: Morgan Stanley · Thoughts on the Market — Morgan Stanley strategists discuss how massive capital expenditures by hyperscalers for AI infrastructure are increasingly influencing the corporate bond market and its relationship to U.S. Treasurys. As companies finance enormous AI-related CapEx needs through corporate debt issuance, this trend is beginning to reshape bond market dynamics beyond traditional Treasury-driven patterns.

item.title: Not Locked Up: Accessing Liquidity in Tax-Aware Portfolios
item.dc:creator: AQR
item.description: AQR · AQR Research & Insights (web) — AQR research examines how investors can access liquidity from tax-aware long-short strategies without fully liquidating positions or sacrificing portfolio characteristics. The study explores methods to generate meaningful cash while maintaining investment exposure and tax efficiency. This approach offers a middle ground between staying fully invested and raising cash through complete portfolio liquidation.
